label: SYNTHETIC_DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY

revision_history.r1: flat-colour end walls + small centered markers. Render-scan (commit be6ba04): geometry gates 1-4,7 PASS, but GATE 6 (embedding distinctness) FAILED (DINO 0.734 goal images / 0.79 center N-vs-W >= 0.60) — branches structurally identical, differ only in hue + small marker.
revision_history.r2: each branch given a distinct SHAPE FAMILY (round/pointed/boxy/cylindrical) + large sign + floor prop + wall pattern. Render-scan (commit 6930b65): geometry still PASS, distinctness improved (center 0.79->0.62, goal images 0.734->0.649) but GATE 6 STILL FAILED (>= 0.60): close goal images were mostly flat wall and all arms shared an identical gray corridor shell that dominated the embedding.
revision_history.r3: branch-specific CORRIDOR SHELL: per-arm tinted side walls (MatWallN/W/E/S), per-arm branch-colour floor strip, per-arm shape-family side-wall relief; goal cameras pulled back to ~2.3 m. Render-scan (commit 201f91b): geometry still PASS but GATE 6 STILL FAILED and WORSENED (center 0.62->0.654, goal images 0.649->0.689). Diagnosis: DINO is sensitive to the SHARED corridor perspective GEOMETRY, not colour/decor; appearance-only changes cannot reach <0.60 for a symmetric cross.
revision_history.r4: per-branch GEOMETRY + dominant FOREGROUND (no metric/threshold change): large branch-specific HIGH objects that dominate the upper goal frame (N sphere, W cone, E cube, S columns; bottom z>=~1.0 m so central depth-openness 3.5 m is preserved), plus the WEST corridor narrowed with inner liner walls (perspective differs from native-width NORTH). Goal images captured at 1.5 m AND 2.0 m standoff; analyze picks the better. Re-run render-scan gates 1-7 only.

purpose: Idealized, authored branch-choice junction to test the H8 goal-conditioned angular branch-selection hypothesis in isolation from scene-sourcing confounds, after five real-world-like Isaac scenes failed the Track-B render-valid-junction gate. A synthetic diagnostic isolates the model/objective question from the (now-exhausted) real-asset geometry question.

frame.yaw_convention_deg: 0=+X (east), CCW positive, so N=90, W=180, S=270

geometry.why_cross_not_T: The Track-B cardinal render-scan classifies a left/right T-junction as COLLINEAR_AISLE_NOT_JUNCTION because its two arms form one straight through-corridor (ns_open XOR ew_open). A 4-way cross makes BOTH axes through-corridors (ns_open==ew_open), so the analyzer treats the center as a junction and the trained branch choice is a genuine PERPENDICULAR pair (90 deg), never a collinear 180 deg pair.

N.identity_r2: big white circular disc sign (high on wall) + 3 dark horizontal industrial stripes + blue sphere floor prop

S.identity_r2: 3 dark vertical bars (flush) + red cylinder floor prop

E.identity_r2: big white square sign + 3 dark checker tiles + orange crate (cube) floor prop

W.identity_r2: big yellow triangular (cone) sign + green cone floor prop + dark chevron cone

geometry.branch_visual_identity_r2_note: R2 gate-6 fix: each branch has a distinct SHAPE FAMILY (round/pointed/boxy/cylindrical), not just a hue + small centered marker, so a structure-focused, largely colour-invariant encoder (DINO) sees genuinely different scenes. Signs sit high on the end wall and wall patterns are flush (depth kept >= 3.0 m); floor props are offset + low so central depth-openness is preserved.
geometry.branch_visual_identity_r3_note: R3 corridor-shell fix: the whole field of view now differs per branch, not just the end wall. Per-arm SIDE WALLS are tinted (N blue, W green, E orange, S red via MatWallN/W/E/S), each arm has a branch-colour FLOOR STRIP, and each arm has a shape-family SIDE-WALL RELIEF (N horizontal bands, W yellow cone pylons, E dark square panels, S dark vertical bars). Goal-image cameras pulled back to ~2.3 m standoff so signs/props/shell are in-frame. Reliefs are flush on walls / flat on floor (off the central column) so central depth-openness stays 3.5 m.
geometry.branch_visual_identity_r4_note: R4 geometry + dominant foreground: each branch gets a LARGE branch-specific object dominating the upper goal frame (N=big blue sphere, W=big green cone, E=big orange cube, S=red columns). Objects sit HIGH (bottom z>=~1.0 m) so from both the junction-centre probe and the goal cameras they are above the central depth band -> central depth-openness (3.5 m) preserved, no near occlusion, navigable branch not hidden. The WEST corridor is narrowed to +/-0.78 with inner liner walls so its perspective geometry differs from the native-width (+/-1.0) NORTH corridor. Goal images rendered at 1.5 m and 2.0 m standoff; the standoff with lower embedding similarity is reported.

safety_envelope.note: All navigable points satisfy |x|,|y| <= 3.5 m, comfortably inside the hardcoded 6.0 m safety watchdog. CL_BOUND_XY is NOT modified.

render_scan_expectation.method: same corrected cardinal render-scan as Track-B (E/N/W/S RGB + distance_to_image_plane depth, DomeLight 1000, robot-eye z=0.47)
render_scan_expectation.open_floor_note: Depths in [3.0,4.0) => open (>=3.0) but below the 4.0 m open-floor threshold => EXPECTED to satisfy the render-valid junction gate, pending render-scan validation (not a result until gates 1-7 run). If arms are lengthened past ~3.9 m the center reads all-4 >= 4.0 => OPEN_FLOOR_NOT_JUNCTION, which then REQUIRES the mandatory gate-5 contact-sheet visual override (a genuine walled cross is verified by eye, not by depth alone).
render_scan_expectation.caveat: Cardinal sampling resolves orthogonal (90 deg) junctions, not oblique forks. Any 60-70 deg Y-variant is NOT confirmable by this scan and must be drive+visual validated only.

trained_branches.collinear_note: The N-S and E-W arms are each collinear pairs. The trained goal pair is ALWAYS perpendicular (A=N, B=W). Never pair N with S or E with W as the two goals — that is the collinear near/far trap the Track-B gate rejects.

start_pose.note: In the south approach corridor, facing north toward the decision point (0,0). The approach corridor is shared by both routes; they diverge only at (0,0).

lighting.target: luma >= 15, low lower-frame black fraction, unoccluded straight corridors

visual_design.dino_distinctness_advisory: ADVISORY ONLY per Outcome A + E (docs/research/H8_TRACK_B_DISTINCTNESS_GATE_DECISION.md, commit 53106f3): DINO cosine(goalA_view, goalB_view) is recorded but is NOT a hard pass/fail gate for this symmetric fork, because the shared corridor perspective dominates DINO on a symmetric cross (it does not separate same-from-distinct). Branch identity still uses distinct hue (blue vs green) AND marker shape (circle vs triangle) AND floor cue (forward vs left arrow), verified by the mandatory contact-sheet visual check.

instance_split_disjoint.rule: Junction instances are DISJOINT across splits. Episodes within a split are drawn only from that split's instances via start-pose jitter. This guarantees no goal image, coordinate, or frame crosses splits.

min_dataset.leakage_rule: No frame, goal image, coordinate, or junction instance may appear in more than one split. Goal images are hashed and instance ids + coordinates checked disjoint before any training.

claim_boundary_statements: It is not real-scene / real-world evidence.
It is not promotion (DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY_NOT_PROMOTED; incumbent retained).
It is not full goal-conditioned ImageNav evidence.
It carries no training authorization (training remains blocked).
CL_BOUND_XY is unchanged (6.0 m watchdog untouched).
One cross is not enough for a leakage-safe train/val/test split (a single junction has only two goal coordinates).
Future training requires a family of at least 6 disjoint junction instances (split by instance; no cross-split reuse of frames/goals/coordinates/instances).
